reena: Hey — noticed the /v1/generate doc has inconsistent request-body examples. The OpenAPI example shows `input: \"...\"` but the JS SDK snippet uses `messages: [{role: 'user', content: '...'}]`. Folks following the JS sample hit a TypeError when the runtime expected chat-style `messages`. Can we align these? cc @kai

sam: Repro'd locally. The server currently accepts both shapes for backward compatibility, but the new chat models expect `messages`. `input` is legacy for text-only models. Docs should prefer `messages` for chat endpoints and include a small migration note showing how to translate `input` -> `messages`.

kai: I can update the node example. Plan: show two minimal snippets — 1) chat-style (recommended) and 2) legacy text-style with a one-line migration example. I'll also update the examples repo file `examples/node/generate.js`.

reena: Please also update the OpenAPI example in the API reference so examples match across SDKs and the curl/python snippets. If you add the migration example, put it under a small heading "Migration from input to messages".

kai: Will do. Draft PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4321 — changes include updated OpenAPI examples, updated JS snippet, added curl & python minimal examples, and a tiny migration note: `// migrate: { input: 'hi' } -> { messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }] }`. I'll add a unit test for the example runner too.

docs-bot: Build status for PR #4321 — docs build passed ✅ preview: https://deploy-preview-4321--docs.redwood.ai/api-reference/generate

maria: One more thing — the doc linter flagged the response schema: `choices` is documented as an object but responses are arrays. We should change the schema to `choices: [ { index, text, delta? } ]` and add a non-streaming vs streaming sample.

sam: Agreed. Suggested sample to include in the response section:
```json
{
  "id": "gen-123",
  "choices": [
    { "index": 0, "text": "Hello there" }
  ]
}
```
Also include a streaming snippet showing `choices[].delta` pieces.

reena: Perfect — once the PR merges I'll update the migration guide page and add a short note in the release notes. Thanks for the quick turnaround. :tada:
